subtitle: What is prayer — and why do Muslims pray five times a day?

title.text: Three ideas to carry with you

spans.text: Prayer is a moment in which a Muslim stands before God. It is a pillar of Islam after the testimony of faith, with set times and a known way.
Muslims pray five times each day and night, as God commanded — like a river at the door, through which He wipes away minor sins.
Their order in a Muslim’s day: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha — each with a time that begins and ends.
